ADJOURNMENT The next regular meeting of the Johnson County Board of Zoning Appeals is scheduled for Tuesday, October 27th, 2026, at 7:00 PM. LIVE STREAMING AVAILABLE HERE Meeting ID: 870 6549 8518 Passcode: 100889 (Link can also be found on the County Website under Events Calendar – Click on Events Website) 2 Staff Report CASE NUMBER: V-07-26 ADDRESS: 5362 Warrior Trail, Whiteland, Parcel #: 41-05-23-041-023.000-033 PETITIONER: Sandhu Properties INC, By Chad Leinart ADDENDUM FOR SEPTEMBER BOARD MEETING The subject property has been cleaned up, and all improper land uses have ceased. All unauthorized materials and activities have been removed from the site, the house has been secured and boarded up, and access points have been blocked to prevent further unauthorized use. The property has remained in full compliance with the Board’s motion and applicable zoning regulations since the June Board of Zoning Appeals meeting. This petition was previously continued by the Board to allow the petitioner time to demonstrate active efforts to abate all unpermitted uses prior to formal approval. Aside from the site cleanup and securing of the property, no other changes or modifications have been submitted regarding the application. All other findings, details, and recommendations in the original Staff Report remain unchanged REQUEST VARIANCE OF USE of the Johnson County Unified Development Ordinance to allow for a trucking parking and trucking facility business (not permitted in a GB-zoned property). PROPERTY DESCRIPTION This variance request involves a 12.696-acre parcel zoned GB (General Business). The property is currently unimproved, though it contains an existing dwelling that is not being used for residential purposes. The land is currently being utilized for parking. Surrounding land uses include: South: Several semi-tractor oriented businesses. North: Semi Parking, Warehouse, and manufacturing uses, including a similar use approved in 2023 by the Board of Zoning Appeals. All affected parcels, with the exception of 5440 Warrior Trail, are located within the Town of Whiteland limits VARIANCE OF USE REQUEST If approved, this Variance of Use request would allow the property to be redeveloped as a commercial truck parking lot, with the potential to repurpose the existing structure for fleet operations. Proposed Site Plan & Operations Parking Capacity: The submitted site plan proposes parking for approximately 71 semi-trucks and semi-trailers. Structure Reuse: The existing structure is proposed to be converted into an office building. 3 Technical Review Adjustments: The final number of parking spots may be reduced during the Technical Review Committee (TRC) review of the civil plans to ensure compliance with development standards, including parking lot setbacks, landscaping, and drainage requirements. Hours of Operation: According to the petitioner’s submitted Plan of Operation, the facility will operate 24 hours a day with security. REGULATORY REQUIREMENTS The development will be required to go through the Technical Review Committee process and must adhere to the following:  All commercial standards in the zoning ordinance.  Procurement of a State Design Release for commercial use of the existing building.  Full compliance with all requirements of the Stormwater Management Ordinance. STAFF NOTES AND RECOMMENDATION This property has been continuously used for truck parking without authorization from staff, despite repeated enforcement notices from the department. However, staff notes that this formal application indicates the property owners are now making an effort to correct past violations and establish a compliant parking facility. If approved, this process will ensure the development is better suited for the area in both appearance and operational use. The existing dwelling on the property has previously been used by the property owner and guests as a social gathering spot, which has presented ongoing issues for the Town of Whiteland. The house is currently unfit for occupation. This unauthorized use must cease immediately, regardless of the outcome of this variance request. The Town of Whiteland has provided an official response to this use request, which is attached to this staff report for review. The requested variance is consistent with and similar to the uses of adjoining properties. Staff recommends the following conditions for consideration: 1. Required Approvals: The development must obtain all required permits and approvals before any improvements are made to the property. 2. Cease Existing Operations: All current semi-truck parking on the property must be removed until proper permits have been issued and site improvements are completed. 3. Structure Occupancy: The existing structure cannot be occupied or used until proper commercial permits have been obtained. 4. Nuisance Mitigation: If the structure is not brought into commercial use within one (1) year of this approval, it must be demolished and removed from the property to deter improper use and prevent a public nuisance. 4 5. Town Interlocal Agreement: The development must include and adhere to all stipulations provided by the Town of Whiteland. STAFF VARIANCE OF USE FINDINGS OF FACT: STAFF ANALYSIS 1. The approval will not be injurious to the public health, safety, morals, and general welfare of the community. The proposed conversion of the property into a secure, 24-hour commercial semi-truck parking facility will not be injurious to the public health, safety, or general welfare, provided all staff conditions are met. The property will undergo a rigorous Technical Review Committee (TRC) process to ensure proper drainage, stormwater management, landscaping, and setbacks are implemented. Furthermore, requiring the unapproved, hazardous use of the existing residential structure to cease and mandating its removal if not developed within one year directly mitigates an existing public nuisance and improves community safety. 2. The use and value of the area adjacent to the property included in the variance will not be affected in a substantially adverse manner. The proposed use is highly consistent with the established character of the immediate area. The property is bordered to the south and north by semi-tractor-oriented businesses. By bringing this site into compliance through formal development standards, the physical appearance and operational safety of the site will be significantly upgraded compared to its current unauthorized state, thereby protecting adjacent property values. 3. The need for the variance does arise from some condition peculiar to the property involved. The 12.696-acre parcel is currently zoned GB (General Business), which does not permit the transportation and logistics support uses that have become dominant in this immediate area. Due to the intense semi-tractor traffic and industrial warehouse operations directly bordering the site to the north and south, it is highly impractical for this property to be developed for any of the retail or light commercial uses standardly permitted in the GB district. The unique physical location of the parcel—effectively locked within a heavy industrial and transportation corridor—creates a distinct peculiarity where standard general business uses are no longer viable or compatible. 4. The strict application of the terms of the Zoning Ordinance will constitute an unnecessary hardship if applied to the property for which variance is sought. Strict adherence to the GB zoning text would restrict the property from fulfilling its most logical economic use as a support facility for the surrounding transport sector. Forcing standard retail or office development on a site locked between semi-truck facilities and manufacturing warehouses creates an unnecessary hardship, as such businesses would struggle with compatibility. Granting the variance allows the petitioner to formalize and legally rectify the land use in a way that matches the market reality of the corridor. 5. The approval does not interfere substantially with the Comprehensive Plan. 5 The Comprehensive Plan’s recommendation for mixed use in this area. Mixed uses development is intended to encourage a well-planned, integrated mix of compatible uses that relate well and support one another. This use is compatible with other uses in the area. GENERAL INFORMATION Applicant: Chad Leinart 3200 Sycamore Ct, Ste 2A Columbus IN 47203 Owner: Sandhu Properties Inc 5362 Warrior Trl Whiteland IN 46143 Zoning: GB Land Use: undeveloped land, parking Future Land Use: Mixed -use ~MNH 6 V-07-26 Base Map subject site 7 V-07-26 Base Map II 8 V-07-26 AERIAL 9 Proposed Plan of Operation, V-07-26 10 V-07-26 Petitioner’s Findings of Facts 11 12 6/11/2026 Members of the Johnson County Board of Zoning Appeals Re: V-07-26 Sandhu Properties INC 5362 Warrior Trail The Town of Whiteland (TOW) has been made aware of the request for a use variance for the property located at 5362 Warrior Trail, which is located in Johnson County. • Warrior Trail, which is owned by the Town of Whiteland, is only designated for 11,000 lbs and is not designated for truck traffic from 790’ north of Whiteland Rd. to the end of Warrior Trail. The road that was put into place for the neighboring parcel at 5440 Warrior Trail was regulated to have no more than 35 trucks. The road has been installed less than 18 months, and that portion of the road is already failing. With an already failing road, adding additional trucks will only add to the problem that has been created by the previous trucking development. See attached photos that were taken on June 9, 2026. • Stormwater. This site, since 2020 has increased impervious surface with no regards to any type of improvements on drainage. • IDEM/County Drainage Board/Municipal permits. As they have seemingly changed the overall layout of the property, have they ever obtained any permits for the improvements that have been made on this parcel? Have they ever reached out to the local jurisdiction for any type of official improvement or inquired about what would be required of them? • The TOW police department has made numerous interactions on this property, and it has created a nuisance in the general area due to exterior condition of the property. This has been a blighted property within our community since the parcel owner has taken ownership. • The increase in truck traffic and the impact that this type of development would have on TOW owned infrastructure would not outweigh the positives that would come from this parcel. They would undoubtedly utilize the existing structure as an “office” but would but would continue to utilize in the same condition and occupancy it currently as a multi-family structure. The Town of Whiteland is concerned that allowing this type of development would ultimately lead to more issues and resources being utilized by our staff than the positives that would come from this type of development where there is already a litany of viable options with parcels to the south to allow for trucking facilities and truck parking. We kindly request that this variance be denied, due to the state statute requirements for being granted a use variance based on IC 36-7-4-918.4 which requires: 1. “The approval will not be injurious to the public health, safety, morals, and general welfare of the community” - This would disproportionally represent the injurious portion to the Town of Whiteland as we have had multiple police resources and code enforcement regarding trash and rubbish in the area. Adding to the additional issues we’ve already seen with the neighboring parcel, this would only add additional trucks and usage on the TOW infrastructure. 2. “the strict application of the terms of zoning ordinance will constitute an unnecessary hardship if applied to the property for which the variance is sought” - Purchasing a property with an intent that 13 does not allow a permitted use of a zoned parcel does not constitute an “unnecessary hardship” rather a lack of planning on behalf of the parcel owner. Based off the Johnson County’s planning department definition within the current UDO states an “unnecessary hardship” Significant economic injury that: a. Arises from the strict application of zoning regulations in this ordinance to the conditions of a particular, existing parcel of property; b. Effectively deprives the parcel owner of all reasonable economic use of the parcel; and c. Is clearly more significant than compliance cost or practical difficulties. Furthermore, the existing structure doesn’t meet the setback requirements for GC zoning in the current UDO which requires front setbacks based off road designation (Collector/Local-40’, Minor Arterial-50’, I/Principal Arterial-60’). If the BZA does approve the use variance we would request the following commitments by the property owner: 1. Improve Warrior Trail with concrete from the Town limits to the end of Warrior Trail. The Town of Whiteland will be submitting for a Community Crossings Matching Grant program this Fall for reconstruction of Warrior Trail from Whiteland Rd to end of Town limits. This road will be converted to all concrete to ensure that it can withstand the truck traffic. 2. Apply for Town of Whiteland curb cut permit Sincerely, Carmen Young Billy Patrick Town Manager Building Commissioner Town of Whiteland Town of Whiteland Cc: Richard Hill, Whiteland Town Council President Derek Cox, Whiteland Town Marshal 14 Warrior Trail (Photos taken 6.9.2026) 15 16 Staff Report CASE NUMBER: V-12-26 ADDRESS: 3.9 acres located at approximately 3855 Olive Branch Road, Greenwood Parcel #: 41-04-11-022-022.000-038 PETITIONER: Story Custom Development LLC, By Eric Prime REQUEST VARIANCE OF USE of the Johnson County Unified Development Ordinance to allow a group home use for senior living (not permitted in an SR, Single Family Residential District) PROPERTY DESCRIPTION This 3.96-acre site is zoned SR (Single Family Residential). The property is currently unimproved grass and surrounded by mature trees and wooded areas. The property is surrounded by residential lots used residentially. Along the south, east, and west side of the property are platted major subdivisions, Brockton Manor and Highland Park. On the north side of Olive Branch Road are similar parcels of land used residentially. VARIANCE REQUEST This Use Variance request seeks approval to operate a residential group home specializing in senior memory care on the subject 3.96-acre tract. Because the Johnson County Unified Development Ordinance (UDO) does not explicitly permit group homes (defined under the UDO as “A non-profit or for-profit group home regulated under IC 31-27 for the sheltered care of persons with special needs, which, in addition to providing food and shelter, may also provide some combination of personal care, social or counseling services, and transportation.”) or nursing homes (defined under the UDO as “An establishment that provides continuous day and night room and board, personal services, and medical care for compensation, for two (2) or more elderly or infirm persons who are not related to the owner/operator of the home.”) as a permitted use within any unincorporated zoning district, a Use Variance is required to establish the use. Staff notes that this petition involves complex intersections between local zoning authority and federal protections of disabled individuals under the Fair Housing Amendments Act (FHAA) and the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA). Local jurisdictions are generally required to provide "reasonable accommodations" to afford persons with disabilities an equal opportunity to use and enjoy a residential dwelling and live in a residentially zoned district. However, recent Indiana trial court proceedings regarding similar facilities— specifically Willow Haven v. Carmel / Nagireddy out of Hamilton County—indicates that federal law does not completely bypass local administrative remedies. The Hamilton County Trial Court recently ruled that federal mandates do not require a municipality to dispense with its standard UDO definitions or enforcement without the petitioner first engaging in local variance procedures. Staff further notes the matter is currently pending with the Indiana Court of Appeals and therefore additional court guidance is not available. Accordingly, this petition is brought before the Johnson County Board of Zoning Appeals (BZA) to formally consider whether the proposed use satisfies both Indiana statutory criteria for a use variance and the framework of a reasonable accommodation under federal law. Petitions Information: 17 The petitioner is proposing a one-story, residential-scale structure to operate as a senior memory care group home, and a detailed Plan of Operation and proposed site plan are attached to this report for further review. The facility will be constructed with standard residential architectural features to match the character of a single-family dwelling, featuring an interior layout of 12 bedrooms, 6 bathrooms, a single residential kitchen, and shared common living spaces. The facility will utilize private, on-site caregiver support to assist residents with daily living needs, though these caregivers will not provide clinical medical support. The structure will not include an attached garage, but the site plan designates 13 on-site parking spaces to accommodate staff, visitors, and support services. Regarding site conditions, a portion of the subject property falls within a FEMA-designated flood zone, but all proposed structural development will occur entirely outside of this area, with the only footprint inside the flood zone being the driveway. Additionally, the property contains several mature trees and established landscaping that currently provide an effective natural buffer between the site and the majority of the abutting residential lots. The petitioner plans to keep all of the trees that don’t need to be removed for the building pad and driveway. It is also anticipated to add more landscaping, primarily around the parking area and front yard. FINDINGS OF FACT: VARIANCE OF DEVELOPMENT STANDARDS State Requirement: The approval will not be injurious to the public health, safety, morals, and general welfare of the community. The proposed use is a residential facility serving senior citizens requiring memory care. In general, these facilities operate under quiet, low-impact conditions similar to standard residential uses. Provided that proper emergency vehicle access, life-safety compliance, and adequate utility capacities are verified, the residential nature of the care home is not likely to cause injury to public health or safety. State Requirement: The use and value of the area adjacent to the property included in the variance will not be affected in a substantially adverse manner. The proposed facility operates as a residential-scale memory care home, which inherently maintains a low- impact operational profile similar to standard single-family neighborhoods. Unlike commercial medical facilities, a small residential group home generates minimal traffic, structured delivery times, and quiet day-to- day operations. The facility will be constructed with similar residential elements which, along with the natural environment, will continue to influence the appearance of residential use to the adjacent areas. State Requirement: The need for the variance arises from some condition peculiar to the property involved. A distinct peculiarity exists within the broader context of the Johnson County zoning framework: the UDO lacks any zoning district where a group home or nursing home is allowed as a permitted use or right. Because the text of the UDO restricts this specific housing type globally across the county's jurisdiction, the terms of the zoning ordinance itself creates a unique regulatory hardship for this specific classification of property use and therefore a condition peculiar to the property involved. State Requirement: The strict application of the terms of the Zoning Ordinance will constitute an unnecessary hardship if applied to the property for which a variance is sought. Strict application of the UDO would entirely prohibit the petitioner from establishing a memory care home anywhere within the unincorporated county. Under federal law (the Fair Housing Act and Americans with Disabilities Act), individuals with cognitive disabilities such as dementia and Alzheimer's are afforded 18 protections that require local governments to make reasonable accommodations in their zoning rules. Completely barring this housing type constitutes an unnecessary hardship and presents significant federal compliance risk. State Requirement: The approval does not interfere substantially with the Comprehensive Plan. The Johnson County Comprehensive Plan generally seeks to preserve residential areas while ensuring diverse housing options exist for all segments of the population, including aging demographics and those with disabilities. While the Comprehensive Plan favors preserving the character of single-family areas, providing structured care for seniors within a residential environment aligns with broader community health goals, provided site-scale impacts are mitigated. Staff Recommendation: Staff recommends the following conditions if the Board makes a motion to approve this request: 1. The Plan of Operation shall be incorporated, including that the front façade of the proposed improvements and landscaping be substantially similar to Figure 1: Story Cottage at Williams Creek, Indianapolis. 2. The Petitioner shall take reasonable measures to preserve healthy mature trees located on the property that serve as a natural buffer between the proposed facility and adjacent properties. .GENERAL INFORMATION Applicant: Strand Associates INC 629 Washington Street Columbus IN 47601 Owner: Story Custom Development LLC 630 3rd Ave. SW Suite 200 Carmel IN 46032 Current Zoning: SR (single-family residential ) Existing Land Use: undeveloped Futu

Myers Representative County Council 1/1/2026 - 12/31/2026 Ron Bates Alternate Member - County Council 1/1/2026 - 12/31/2026 Greg Cantwell Surveyor - Office Held Office Term Shalee Bradley ANR County Extension Agent - Office Held Office Term Charles Canary Citizen Member appointed by County Commissioners 1/1/2023 - 12/31/2027 Douglas Gray Citizen Member appointed by County Commissioners 1/1/2024 - 12/31/2027 Steven Hickman Citizen Member appointed by County Commissioners 1/1/2023 - 12/31/2027 Robert Page Citizen Member appointed by County Commissioners 1/1/2024 - 12/31/2027 Stoney Vann Citizen Member appointed by County Commissioners 1/1/2025 - 12/31/2028 UNIFIED DEVELOPMENT ORDINANCE – 2026 Amendment proposal The Department of Planning and Zoning has prepared a series of proposed text amendments to the Johnson County Uniﬁed Development Ordinance (UDO). Following the comprehensive adoption of the UDO in 2024, staff have identiﬁed several areas requiring technical cleanup, administrative clariﬁcation, and legislative updates. The proposed changes cover key operational areas including statutory protections for shooting ranges, deﬁned standards for event centers and group homes, clariﬁcation of accessory dwelling unit and structure sizes, and relief from suburban standards (such as sidewalks and individual lot landscaping) in rural and agricultural zoning districts.  Draft Redline Version of UDO Amendments as of 8-14-26  List of track changes to the UDO Below is the only amendment that was not voted on from the August meeting Group Home and Nursing Homes Rationale: Updates were made to the group home standards to align county zoning regulations better with ADA and federal fair housing guidelines, while resolving internal code inconsistencies across residential zoning districts. Deﬁnition & Scale: The UDO explicitly distinguishes a Group Home from larger institutional facilities, such as commercial nursing or convalescent centers. This distinction ensures group homes operate within a typical residential scale and character. State Compliance: Standards were updated to reference appropriate state licensing bodies—speciﬁcally the Division of Disability and Rehabilitative Services (DDRS) and the Division of Mental Health and Addiction (DMHA)—ensuring local oversight supports, rather than conﬂicts with, state licensing mandates. Permitted Districts & Occupancy Caps: Clariﬁed standards across residential and agricultural districts. Occupancy remains capped at eight (8) residents (excluding support staff) to maintain compatibility with single-family residential neighborhoods while ensuring compliance with federal Fair Housing Act protections for group living arrangements. Permitting & Review Process: Streamlined the review framework to clarify when a facility is permitted by right versus when it requires special approval, eliminating previous ambiguity surrounding unlisted uses or special exception requirements for state-licensed residential care homes. Affected Sections: Pages 15, 17,,19,21,23,27 105, 112,236,238,240, and Appendix A. 15 2. Agricultural District (AG). a. Purpose. The purpose of this district is to provide for and protect substantial areas for a broad variety of agricultural uses where little or no urbanization has occurred or is planned to occur. The district intentionally limits broad residential uses to provide for large areas of contiguous farm land. b. Land Uses. Greenhouse / Nursery. All sales must be products created and/or produced on-site. Oﬀ- site shipments of products to the site are expressly prohibited. 23.24. Heavy Equipment Sales and Rentals. a. All equipment stored outside the principal business shall: 1) Be located on an asphalt or concrete surface; 112 proposed sand and gravel mining pit. The sampling and analysis plan shall contain speciﬁc information, including: 1) Site Background; 2) Sample Location Points; 3) Monitoring parameters (at a minimum, this should include regulated drinking water metals and organic and inorganic primary and secondary drinking water parameters regulated by IDEM under 327 IAC 8 and the Environmental Protection Agency for Public Water Supply Systems, and any other contaminants required by the Johnson County Planning Department); 4) Analytical methods (analysis shall be by a laboratory certiﬁed to perform the analysis utilizing the most recent test methods and regulatory limits); 5) Detection limits; 6) Sampling personnel; 7) Decontamination procedures; 8) Water level measurement and purging; 9) Sample collection procedures and preservation; 10) Quality control; 11) Sample management; 12) Chain of custody; and 13) Sampling event reporting e. Reclamation Plan. A reclamation plan which outlines the scope, scale, and cost of associated remediation to enable the aﬀected land use to be reused. 39. Nursing Home a. Nursing homes shall be licensed by the Indiana State Department of Health and obtain, comply with, and maintain any required license from the Johnson County Health Department. b. Nursing homes in dwelling districts shall be designed to be residential in character. e.c.Nursing homes shall be designed with appropriate access and maneuverability for emergency vehicles 38.40. Oﬃce, General. In the PR District, the use is limited to oﬃce space secondary to another land use that is allowed within the PR District. 39.41. Place of Public Assembly, Indoor. A minimum lot size of two (2) acres shall be required for the use to locate on the property. 40.42. Recreational Vehicle Park and Campground. 239 GROUP HOME: A residential structure or facility where six (6) or more unrelated persons who are in need of care, support or supervision can live together, such as children or those who are elderly, disabled or mentally ill. Group Homes housing persons with developmental disabilities shall obtain, comply with, and maintain a license from the Indiana Division of Disability and Rehabilitative Services. Group Homes housing those living with psychiatric disorders or addictions shall obtain, comply with, and maintain a license from the Indiana Division of Mental Health and Addictions . A non-proﬁt or for- proﬁt group home regulated under IC 31-27 for the sheltered care of persons with special needs, which, in addition to providing food and shelter, may also provide some combination of personal care, social or counseling services, and transportation. GUARANTEE: Cash, bonds, or similar ﬁnancial instruments deposited with the County to ensure that required improvements will be constructed or installed. HEAVY EQUIPMENT SALES AND RENTALS: A business engaged in the rental or sales of powered heavy mechanical equipment. HEIGHT: The distance from the ground where the structure stands to the highest point of the structure. HOME BUSINESS: A lawful activity conducted for ﬁnancial gain, where such use does not include the sale of goods to customers on the premises or opening of the home to the public for the sale of goods or services without an invitation or appointment. The use diﬀers from a home occupation in that mechanical equipment related to the use may be stored outside of the building provided that proper screening is provided. Minimal traﬃc shall be required to occur on the property so that there is minimal disruption to the neighborhood. HOME OCCUPATION: An occupation, profession, domestic craft, or economic enterprise which is customarily conducted in a residential dwelling. The use diﬀers from a home business in that there shall be no outside indication that a business is operated on the site. HOMEOWNER’S ASSOCIATION: A formally constituted non-proﬁt association or corporation made up of the property owners and/or residents of a deﬁned area; who collectively may take permanent responsibility for costs and upkeep of commonly owned or designated community property. HOSPITAL / REHABILITATIVE CARE: An institution providing primary health services and medical or surgical care to persons, primarily inpatients, suﬀering from illness, disease, injury, disability, and other physical or mental conditions and including, as an integral part of the institution, related facilities, such as laboratories, outpatient facilities, training facilities, medical oﬃces, and staﬀ residences. This includes a clinic, hospital, or sanitarium, except a criminal, mental, or animal hospital; and nursing or convalescent home. HOTEL: A commercial building in which lodging is provided and oﬀered to the public for compensation. IMPROVEMENT LOCATION PERMIT (ILP): A certiﬁcate issued under this UDO permitting a person to erect, construct, enlarge, alter, repair, move, improve, remove, convert, or demolish any building or structure within its jurisdiction or to change the use or condition of the land. 254 Appendix A, Land Use Matrix Residential Uses by Zoning District Table A.1, Land Use Matrix: Residential Uses -- = Prohibited; P = Permitted; US = Use Standards; SE = Special Exception Land Use Parks / Agricultural Residential Commercial Industrial PR AG AR SR DR MR MH GC HC IN Residential PR AG AR SR DR MR MH GC HC IN Single-Family Detached Dwelling -- P P P P P P -- -- -- Duplex (2 du) -- -- -- -- P P -- -- -- -- Townhouse (3 to 10 du) -- -- -- -- -- P -- SE -- -- Apartment (> 3 du) -- -- -- -- -- P -- SE -- -- Manufactured Home Park -- -- -- -- -- -- US -- -- -- Nursing Home P P Group Home SE SE SE SE US US Retirement Housing -- -- -- -- -- SE -- SE -- -- Residential Accessory PR AG AR SR DR MR MH GC HC IN Accessory Structure US US US US US US US US US US Accessory Dwelling Unit, Attached -- US US US -- -- -- -- -- -- Accessory Dwelling Unit, Detached -- US US US -- -- -- -- -- -- Commercial Uses of the Home PR AG AR SR DR MR

items.title: Council Minutes 3-9-2026
items.text: COUNTY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING —MARCH 9, 2026 The meeting was called to order by Council President, Michele Ann Graves. A. Call the Meeting to Order 1. Roll Call The following members were present: Jonathan Myers, John Mailers, Pamela Burton, John Ditmers, and Ron Bates. Melinda Griesemer was absent. 2. Invocation Mrs. Burton gave the invocation. 3. Pledge of Allegiance Mrs. Graves led the Pledge of Allegiance. 4. Approval of 3/9/26 Agenda Mrs. Graves stated the two following changes to the agenda: 1. Remove item C9 General Fund (#1001-0159)Comm Corr/Adult 2. Item C7d should be 1123.11453.00000.0220 -Supp-Asst Director Mr. Bates made a motion to approve the agenda as amended. Mr. Ditmars seconded the motion, which unanimously carried. 5. Public Comments (agenda items only, limited to 5 minutes per person) There were no public comments. B. Routine Matters - Consent Agenda By a single motion, the Board approves the following items, which may include Salary Ordinance Amendments, Additional Appropriations, Reductions, and Transfers. Any items listed on the consent agenda may be removed by a Council member and moved to the regular agenda. Mr. Myers made a motion to approve the consent agenda as presented. Mr. Mallers seconded the motion, which unanimously carried. I. Approval of 2/9/26 Regular Meeting Minutes 2. 93.069 CRI BP2 2025-2026 (#8228) Health (a) From: 8228.36200.00000.0210 Communications $ (720.00) To: 8228.42000.00000.0210 Operating Equipment $ 320.00 To: 8228.25801.00000.0210 Food (new) $ 400.00 3. Park Non-Reverting Capital Improv (#1178) Park (a) AA: 1178.42001.00000.0271 Building & Land Improvement $ 265,746.00 4. Park Non-Reverting Operating (#1179) Park (a) AA: 1179.42001.00000.0273 Building & Land Improvement $ 225,000.00 5. Phelps Charitable Fund (#4113) Park (a) AA: 4113.42000.00000.0128 Operating Equipment $ 15,307.85 (b) AA: 4113.32001.00000.0128 Promotional (new) $ 2,122.37 Council Regular Meeting Minutes — March 9, 2026 Page 1 of 12 6. VASIA 2026 (#9129) VASIA (a) AA: 9129.32000.00000.0133 Dues & Subscriptions $ 2,000.00 (b) AA: 9129.36102.00000.0133 Contractual Services $ 59,210.00 (c) AA: 9129.25801.00000.0133 Food $ 2,100.00 (d) AA: 9129.21001.00000.0133 Volunteer Favors $ 2,000.00 (e) AA: 9129.31500.00000.0133 Travel & Training $ 4,690.00 7. Enhanced Access (#1154) Recorder (a) AA: 1154.36102.00000.0104 Contractual Services $ 1,750.00 8. Prosecutor Hub Grant 2024-2025 (#9133) Prosecutor (a) AA: 9133.14200.00000.0108 Fica-Social Security 166.91 (b) AA: 9133.14300.00000.0108 PERF 251.38 (c) AA: 9133.19900.00000.0108 Overtime $ 2,182.31 (d) AA: 9133.19500.00000.0108 Grant Reimb for Personnel $ 256.71 9. Prosecutor Hub Grant 2026 (#9164) Prosecutor (a) AA: 9164.14200.00000.0108 Fica-Social Security $ 1,530.00 (b) AA: 9164.14300.00000.0108 PERF $ 2,240.00 (c) AA: 9164.19900.00000.0108 Overtime $ 16,230.00 10. Grants Awarded/Non-Governmental (#4300-0155) Sheriff (a) AA: 4300.31500.00000.0155 Travel & Training $ 2,602.00 C. Salary Ordinance Amendments, Additional Appropriations, Reductions, and Transfers 1. Pretrial Diversion Program (#2509) Prosecutor Michelle Murray, Office Administrator, was present to request an additional appropriation to close this grant out. Mrs. Graves asked if this is needed due to overspending the grant. Mrs. Murray replied, she doesn't think it was overspending but isn't sure since it was prior to her time; she just knows this is needed to close out the grant. Mrs. Graves noted the request letter stated it was to correct a negative balance in this fund. She then asked if there were precautions in place to prevent grant funds from running in the red moving forward. Mrs. Murray stated they are trying to make revisions as they go and make corrections as they see them. Mr. Ditmars made a motion to approve the request as presented. Mr. Bates seconded the motion, which carried unanimously. (la) AA: 2509.30060.00000.0286 Grant Adjustments $ 1,032.53 Mrs. Murray was also present to request a part-time hourly rate to $26.50 for a part-time paralegal, which equals the same hourly rate of their full-time paralegals. She noted they would like to hire a part-time person, who has paralegal experience to work in their Pretrial Diversion programs. Mrs. Burton asked what was the maximum they budgeted at budget time and if this amount was over what they initially said their margins would be. Council Regular Meeting Minutes — March 9, 2026 Page 2 of 12 Mrs. Murray answered, yes, they initially budgeted $25.00/hr. Mrs. Burton then stated this would be new money then, an adjustment to the actual budget. Mrs. Murray replied yes; however, right now they are not asking for any additional appropriations in this specific line item. Mrs. Graves noted she did a little bit of research. In 2025, they budgeted $36,000 in this line item and spent $30,347. In 2026, $36,000 was budgeted again; she then asked if it is anticipated to need more money in this line item due to hiring this additional part time person. Mrs. Murray replied she hoped not; this person will be only working two days a week, and not every week. Mrs. Graves stated that Council prefers these types of requests be made at budget time and inquired why this one got overlooked. Mrs. Murray explained they were unaware at budget time they needed help in this area; however, due to some turnover of employees, they are trying to fill this position with part time help instead of full time. Mr. Myers asked why they need help in this area at this increased rate. Mrs. Murry answered by hiring someone with prior paralegal experience, saves them a lot of time training. They are behind due to the volume of cases they have. Mrs. Graves stated that Council would like to see part time job descriptions; she would like those sent to Taylor Webster, Assistant County Attorney for review. Mr. Mallers made a motion to approve the request as presented. Mr. Myers seconded the motion, which carried 5-1; Mrs. Burton voted nay. (1 b) 2509.11400.00000.0286 — Part Time — request approval to increase part time rate from $25.00 to $26.50 2. General Fund (#1001-0201) Highway 3. LIT Economic Development (#1112-0201) Highway Luke Mastin, Supervisor, was present for several requests. Mr. Mastin stated the first two items are the re- appropriations of the cash savings that has been set aside for the Smith Valley Road Project. Last year, it was recommended to do this method of re-appropriation, instead of encumbering, so that it doesn't show twice in the County's Fiscal Plan that their financial advisor Mike Reuter prepares each year. Mr. Bates asked when this comes to fruition, does the State kick in any money. Mr. Mastin replied there is no State money for this project. He explained the bulk of the expense will come from the bond; once the bond is complete, expenses will be paid from these two line items. Mr. Mallers inquired if the bond issuance has occurred yet. Mr. Mastin replied yes; it happened in October 2025. Mr. Mallers then asked what the general timeline looks like for this project. Council Regular Meeting Minutes — March 9, 2026 Page 3 of 12 Mr. Mastin explained they are neck deep in development; they are in the right-of-way acquisition process right now, which will be a long process. They have started seeing some of the appraisals come through and they are moving forward. Mr. Bates asked if this was from St Rd 135 to the interstate. Mr. Mastin replied yes. More specifically, it is from the Mullinix Road round-about to Restin Road (the entrance to Carefree South). They are also coordinating with INDOT, who is designing an intersection improvement project at Smith Valley and St Rd 135, to make sure these two projects tie into together. Mr. Ditmars wanted to clarify that the use of the bond funds will be used first and then these two line items, noting these amounts most likely will carry over to 2027. Mr. Mastin concurred. Mrs. Burton made a motion to approve the two following requests as presented: (2a) AA: 1001.49152.00000.0201 Smith Valley Road (3a) AA: 1112.49152.00000.0201 Smith Valley Road Mr. Mailers seconded the motion, which unanimously carried. 4. Cumulative Bridge #1135) Highway Mr. Mastin was also present for these requests. Mrs. Graves asked to take items 4a & 4b separately. $12,000,000.00 $15,000,000.00 Mr. Mastin stated the request is for a part time engineer that was discussed toward the end of last year. He does have a part time engineer job description (was in February council packet). He stated they hired a part time engineer last year and it is working out great. He noted the bulk of the work they are doing is bridge and culvert related; therefore, they should be paid from this fund. Mrs. Graves stated since this fund is new again for 2026, there was really no Part Time line item to work with. She then inquired how he came up with the amount of $65,000 for this position. Mr. Mastin answered $65,000 was just a rough estimate for work done on an annual part time basis. In reality, he feels like it will be less than that. He also stated during a recent conversation with Mrs. Graves, that when this matter was discussed last year, he had stated about $40,000 a year would be needed and he was fine with lowering his request to the $40,000. He added at budget time he would re-evaluate how much actually should be budgeted for next year. Mr. Ditmars asked what the status was regarding hiring someone for this position. Mr. Mastin replied he hired someone and they started working in December. This person has brought a lot of knowledge, especially on the drainage side and the bridge and culvert side, which has been a significant help to them. Mr. Ditmars then asked what the number should be; an amount should be known since the person has been working since December. Mr. Mastin explained he has paying this position from the MVH Fund, but is requesting it be paid from the Cumulative Bridge Fund. The amount would be the maximum of that $40,000 for the remainder of the year. He will monitor the hours of this employee, who is semi-retired and only working part time. Council Regular Meeting Minutes — March 9, 2026 Page 4 of 12 Mrs. Graves asked if the part time job description has been given to legal. Mr. Mastin replied yes. Mr. Ditmars made a motion to approve the request as revised. Mr. Bates seconded the motion, which carried unanimously. (4a) AA: 1135.11400.00000.0206 Part Time $ 65,000.00 40,000.00 (4b) 1135.11400.00000.0206 — Part Time - approval of $65.00/hr for a part time Engineer Mr. Myers inquired about cash flow since there are so many ongoing projects and asked when they would be completed. Mr. Mastin stated there was a resolution done at the beginning of the year to do a temporary loan from the Rainy Day Fund to the Cumulative Bridge Fund to help with cash flow. Realistically, several of these projects listed below won't be realized until the middle of the year or the end of the year. Additionally, some of these projects are also budgeted in another fund. He does not foresee any cash flow issues. Next, Mr. Mastin explained that all the additional appropriations are being requested to transition funding for upcoming phases of bridge projects already underway from the General Fund and the Cumulative Capital Fund. He noted all of these projects were listed in the February memo, except for the last two items. He stated they recently learned they were awarded federal funding to the Bridge 36 and Bridge 63 Projects that they applied for; however, he doesn't know exactly what the consulting contracts will be yet, so he just estimated a round number so the projects can begin. Mr. Myers made a motion to approve the requests as presented. Mr. Mailers seconded the motion, which unanimously carried. (4c) AA: 1135.34400.00000.0206 Bridge Maint/Repair $ 250,000.00 (4d) AA: 1135.49305.00000.0206 Bridge 66 $ 50,000.00 (4e) AA: 1135.49306.00000.0206 Bridge 98 $ 30,000.00 (41) AA: 1135.48205.00000.0206 Bridge 61 $ 25,000.00 (4g) AA: 1135.49302.00000.0206 Bridge 602 $ 150,000.00 (4h) AA: 1135.49307.00000.0206 Bridge 85 $ 500,000.00 (4i) AA: 1135.49308.00000.0206 Bridge 103 $ 20,000.00 (4j) AA: 1135.49309.00000.0206 Bridge 206 $ 55,000.00 (4k) AA: 1135.49310.00000.0206 Bridge 56 $ 85,000.00 (41) AA: 1135.49503.00000.0206 Bridge Construction/Reconst $ 870,000.00 (4m) AA: 1135.48206.00000.0206 Bridge 36 $ 200,000.00 (4n) AA: 1135.48207.00000.0206 Bridge 63 $ 200,000.00 5. County Highway (#1176) Highway Mr. Mastin was also present for this request. He explained the amount being requested is actually the amount that was remaining in this line item at the end of 2025; he is just re-appropriating it for 2026. Mr. Ditmars made a motion to approve the request as presented. Mrs. Burton seconded the motion, which unanimously carried. (5a) AA: 1176.44100.00204.0201 Misc Equipment $ 422,470.00 Council Regular Meeting Minutes - March 9, 2026 Page 5 of 12 6. Bridge 85 2211 FFE (#9203) Highway Lastly, Mr. Mastin was also present for this request. He explained this will create a new grant line item for their Bridge 85 Project. He noted this project has MPO federal exchange dollars that was provided by the Indianapolis MPO. The bid for this project will be done at the next Commissioners' meeting. Mr. Ditmars asked if it was dollar for dollar. Mr. Mastin replied it was 80% of what they applied for, noting the cost estimate for the project might be lower than what they originally thought. If the bids come in lower, then they will have to return some of these funds. They will only receive 80% of actual expenditures. Mrs. Burton made a motion to approve the request as presented. Mr. Ditmars seconded the motion; the motion carried unanimously. (6a) AA: 9203.49307.00000.0206 Bridge 85 $ 1,682,023.00 7. Comm Corr CTP (#1123) Court Services *retro to 2/5/26* Steve Kermode, Assistant Director, was present to request additional appropriations in this fund, moving them from another fee fund due to a low cash balance. He explained this occurs about every few years. Mrs. Burton made a motion to approve the request as presented. Mr. Bates seconded the motion that carried unanimously. (7a) AA: 1123.11437.00000.0220 Supp-Prob Off/Quality Assur Dir $ 8,461.60 (7b) 1123.11437.00000.0220 — Supp-Prob Off/Quality Assur Dir — Annual Salary of $10,000 (max bi-weekly pay of $384.62 (7c) AA: 1123.11453.00000.0220 Supp-Assist Director $ 8,461.60 (7d) 1123.11437 11453. 00000.0220 Supp Prob Off/Quality Assur Dir Supp-Assist Director — Annual Salary of $10,000 (max bi-weekly pay of $384.62) (7e) AA: 1123.14200.00000.0220 Fica-Social Security $ 1,294.56 (7J AA: 1123.14300.00000.0220 PERF $ 1,895.36 8. Adult Probation Adm Fees (#2001) Court Services Mr. Kermode was also present to request an additional appropriation to cover the cost of a grant that was overspent. He explained this grant ended in September 2025; however, they erroneously forgot to send over a change form to payroll to change where this employee was being paid from. Since then, they have consolidated some things and now everything will go through him, with hopes of preventing this situation again. Now, they have to repay the grant and are paying it from fund #2001 Adult Probation Adm Fees, which is the same fund the employee should have been moved to and paid from when the grant ended. Mrs. Graves stated, for clarification, we have another grant fund in the red. Mr. Kermode answered yes. Mrrs. Graves then asked what is Mr. Kermode's title. Mr. Kermode replied Assistant Director of Community Corrections. Mrs. Graves stated this request says it is for Adult Probation. She then asked if Mr. Kermode was wearing two hats since he has come before the Council with so many bookkeeping errors, asking if doing services for both Community Corrections and Probation could be contributing to some of these accounting errors. Council Regular Meeting Minutes — March 9, 2026 Page 6 of 12 Mr. Kermode replied no; he feels like they had multiple people doing multiple things and now everything will be funneling through him more. Mr. Ditmars asked if this was a carry-over from the restructure that happened a few years ago. Mr. Kermode answered yes, noting this is the last of those issues that just fell through the crack. Mr. Ditmars made a motion to approve the request as presented. Mrs. Burton seconded the motion, which unanimously carried. (8a) AA: 2001.30060.00000.0138 Grant Adjustments $ 19,111.40 9. General Fund (#1001-0159) Comm Corr/Adult This item was removed from the agenda. (9a) AA: 1001.10010.00000.0159 Case Manager Supervisor $ 43,545.05 (9b) 1001.10010.00000.0159 Case Manager Supervisor Annual Salary of $55,862 [max bi weekly pay of $2, 48.54} (9c) AA: 1001.11110.00000.0159 Case Manager (1) $ 39,692.36 (9d) 1001.11110.00000.0159 Case Manager (1) Annual Salary of $43,000 [max bi weekly pay of $1653.85 10. LIT Correctional/Rehab Facilities (#1123-0124) Sheriff/Jail Andy Barnhart, Chief Deputy, was present for this request; however, he asked to first give a brief update on their Merit Deputy hiring process. Mrs. Graves agreed, as long as it was kept brief, due to the lengthy agenda. Mr. Barnhart stated they successfully completed the most recent hiring process for Merit Deputies. He noted they had an outstanding number of applicants and feels like that is a testament to the work the Council has done over the last few years getting the salaries caught up to where they need to be. They ended up with a list of 15 people on the eligibility list, which is triple the amount they had the last time. The Council members thanked Mr. Barnhart for sharing this good news with them. Mr. Barnhart then stated they are requesting four new salary line items, which would technically be permanent temporary line items. This would give the department flexibility to cover shifts when employees go on military leave. They currently have one employe that is on military leave, whose leave keeps getting extended and another employee who is getting ready to go on military leave. He noted they have two other employees who might also be going on military leave as well. He explained when these employees go on leave, they have to keep their job for them, and only have to pay them for 15 military days. When this situation occurs, they would transfer funds from the full time line items into these new temporary line items, so no new money would be needed. He also stated when they hire for these temporary line items they will tell the people these are not guaranteed positions because when the employees comes back from military service, they get their job back. Mrs. Graves noted she also talked to Sheriff Duane Burgess about this request and verified that they are required to hold the positions for the employees who are away on active duty. Mr. Maller made a motion to approve the following request as presented. Mr. Bates seconded the motion, which unanimously carried. Approval of Resolution 2026-03: A Resolution of the Johnson County Council Approving the Execution of a Lease By and Between the Nineveh Fire Protection District, Johnson County, Indiana, and the Nineveh Fire Protection District Building Corporation for the Purpose of Funding the Construction of a New Fire Station Facility for the Nineveh Fire Protection District, Johnson County, Indiana Jeff Peters, from Peters Franklin and serving as the Municipal Advisor on the bonds for the Nineveh Fire Protection District (Nineveh FPD), was present for this request. He stated that the bond counsel and a member of the Nineveh FPD Board were also present. Mr. Peters stated this was first brought to the Council's attention last August. He explained this project started back in 2020; the fire district wants to replace its fire house, which was built in 1965 and won't house a modern fire truck. He stated it is well beyond its useful life and they are working on getting it replaced. There has been a lot of debate and input from taxpayers. The total project cost is now down to $4,070,000; the financing for this will be 20 years. The property tax repayments will begin in pay 2028, with the last payment to be made in January 2048. He explained the reason for the delay is because the amount of these bonds verses the current tax base in this area requires it to be set up as a lease rental with a building corporation. This is similar to what schools must do and what the County did last year with their Redevelopment Authority bonds (the Redevelopment Authority is basically the building corporation for the Redevelopment Commission). Mr. Peters stated when this is put on the tax rolls, it is estimated to be about 9.2 cents. He then gave the example: a homestead property assessed at $250,000, this would cost them about $116.00 a year. Mrs. Graves asked if this is the project that started with a $12 million+ number. Mr. Peters replied yes; however, that number was based on what they thought should be built to face current and future needs. It also included the cost of a new fire truck. He stated the fire truck has been removed from the current project cost and the project has been scaled back to what the fire district and taxpayers think will serve their needs. Brief discussion was held regarding the area where the station is located and the assessed values associated with it; more specifically how it affects the property taxes. Mr. Myers stated he would like to hear from the fire department on what this is going to do for them. Kevin Hendrickson, President of the Nineveh FPD, was present and stated he couldn't speak for the fire department, but from his perspective as a retired firefighter, this will improve a lot of things. First, just the building itself - when they look to buy equipment, they have to spec it because it just won't house what is out there and available today. Second, when it freezes outside, their building freezes and the toilets freeze. There is water in the bay; there is mold and just a ton of issues with the building itself. He then stated with the evacuation systems that are out there today to keep Council Regular Meeting Minutes — March 9, 2026 Page 8 of 12 the carcinogens off the fire fighters, this new facility will house that and improve their health. As far as their equipment goes, that is another hurdle they will need to jump through, being diligent with that funding when buying a new fire truck. Mrs. Burton commented she and a few other council members spent an afternoon at the current fire station in Nineveh, and in her opinion, it is as bad as it can get and doesn't know how it hasn't been condemned yet. She commends the firefighters for making it work. Mr. Ditmars agreed something needs to be done, but there is nothing they can do regarding the democratic process in that geographical area. It is at a point now where both the taxpayers and the district are in agreement on an amount. He doesn't feel like the people are happy with the tax increase, but understand the need for the service it provides. Mrs. Burton expressed the County Council is just the governing body for this; they have no input on what happens - is that correct? Max Adams, from Barnes & Thornburgh and serving as the bond counsel for the Nineveh FPD, was present to explain that the County Council's role outside of the annual appropriations and budgeting is to approve the lease/bond issuance. The project being presented by the BFPD would not increase taxes for the Bargersville Fire District or the County. With recent concerns expressed regarding the transparency of their Board came as a shock to them; however, as a District Board, they want their community and County Officials to feel 100% informed and to be comfortable with their projects' facts. Johnson County Council Pay Philosophy Mrs. Graves stated she had emailed an updated pay philosophy of the Johnson County Council to all members earlier for their review and consideration. She asked for this pay philosophy to be put up on the screen for all to view. She then asked if anyone had any questions. She noted the only significant thing that changed from their prior pay philosophy was regarding the verbiage of longevity pay — which was voted on last month by the Council to not pursue Council Regular Meeting Minutes — July 13, 2026 Page 6 of 11 longevity pay for 2027 due to the future fiscal forecast being so dim. Below is the Johnson County Council Pay Philosophy: Johnson County Council is committed to a fair, transparent, and .fiscally responsible that reflects the values of public service and the conservative stewardship of taxpayer dollars. Our immediate objectives regarding employee pay are: -consistent base pay within similar job classifications in compliance with study, -annual cost of living adjustment, -establish salary ranges to provide a uniform structured progression for and -create a foundation of consistent pay that sets the groundwork for implementing county employees in future budget cycles. Our pay philosophy is based on the following principles: - Internal Equity: ensure employees in similar roles with similar qualifications are compensated fairly and consistently. - Market Awareness: strive for compensation levels that are competitive government - Transparency: employee pay decisions are made in open meetings, in public access laws. - Sustainability: make pay decisions supporting long-term budgetary financial maintaining staffing levels and expertise needed to effectively serve the community. Mr. Bates made a motion to approve the Johnson County Council Pay Philosophy seconded the motion, which unanimously carried. 2. 2027 Budget Guidelines Mrs. Graves stated she had emailed this document to the Council members last week. was based upon the Council's discussion at their June 8, 2026 meeting. A lot of this document originated from the hard work of Mrs. Burton. Mrs. Graves then updated it based on the conversations from the Council's June meeting. She then sent it to the County's legal department for their review, and then it was sent out to all Council members for their review prior to tonight's meeting to assist with discussion points and getting it done in a timely fashion. items.title: Ordinance 2026-O-7: An Ordinance Amending Title 25 of the Johnson County Code of Ordinances
items.text: ORDINANCE NO. 2026-O-7 AN ORDINANCE AMENDING TITLE 25 OF THE JOHNSON COUNTY CODE OF ORDINANCES WHEREAS, Indiana Code§ 36-1-3 et. seq. permits any unit in the State of Indiana to exercise any power or to perform any function necessary to the public interest in the context of its governmental or internal affairs, which is not prohibited by the Constitution of the United States or of the State of Indiana, or denied or pre-empted by any other law, or is not expressly granted by any other law to another governmental entity; and WHEREAS, the Board of Commissioners of Johnson County, Indiana is the executive body under Ind. Code § 36-2-2-2 and is by law authorized to adopt ordinances for the protection of the public health, safety, and general welfare of its residents; and WHEREAS, the purpose of this Ordinance is to regulate peddling in Johnson County and clarify the penalties for violations of this Chapter BE IT THEREFORE ORDAINED BY THE BOARD THAT: Johnson County Code § 25-2-1-4 be amended as follows: § 25-2-1-4 GENERAL PROHIBITIONS; PENALTIES. (A) No person shall: 1. With or without a license, enter upon private property where any form of sticker or sign is clearly displayed advising that the occupant does not wish to be called upon by peddlers, canvassers, and/or solicitors, such as a “No Soliciting” sign; 2. With or without a license, remove any sign or sticker that gives notice that the occupant does not wish to be called upon by peddlers, canvassers, and/or solicitors; 3. With or without a license, distribute any commercial or non-commercial literature at any private property in a manner that causes permanent damage to such property; or 4. With or without a license, remain on private property after being asked by the occupant to leave. COMMISSIONERS Brian P. Baird, Chairman, 2025-2028 Kevin M. Walls, Member, 2023-2026 Ronald H. West, Member, 2025-2028 County Attorney Tiffany M. Costley Assistant County Attorney Taylor E. Webster ADDRESS 86 West Court Street Franklin, Indiana 46131 Phone (317) 346-4300 Fax (317) 736-8066 Website: www.johnsoncounty.in.gov BOARD OF COMMISSIONERS JOHNSON COUNTY ORDINANCE NO. 2026-O-7 AN ORDINANCE AMENDING TITLE 25 OF THE JOHNSON COUNTY CODE OF ORDINANCES Any person violating the provisions of this Subsection (A) may be subject to criminal penalties under Indiana Code. (B) No person shall: 1. With or without a license, use, or attempt to use, any entrance other than the front or main entrance to the dwelling except by express invitation of the occupant of the property; or 2. Engage in peddling activities as defined above without first obtaining a license from the Johnson County Sheriff’s Office. Any person violating the provisions of this Subsection (B) shall be subject to the following fines (escalation on a calendar year basis): First Offense: $50.00 Second Offense: $150.00 Third Offense: $300.00 Subsequent Offenses: $1,000.00 Multiple citations may be issued on the same day, if more than one offense occurs. Repeat

items.title: Notice of Availability of ADA Self-Evaluation and Transition Plan 8/31/26 thru 9/15/26 and Public Meeting on 9/14/26
items.text: NOTICE OF AVAILABILITY OF ADA SELF-EVALUATION AND TRANSITION PLAN & PUBLIC MEETING Johnson County has conducted a Self-Evaluation of all County-owned facilities and all County programs for compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) and prepared a draft Transition Plan describing the results of the self-evaluation. Title II of the ADA requires that each of the County’s services, programs, and activities be readily accessible and usable by individuals with disabilities. Copies of the draft Self-Evaluation and Transition Plan will be available for public review at the following locations in Franklin between August 31st, 2026, and September 15th, 2026.  County Annex (Commissioners/ADA Coordinator’s Office) -86 W. Court St, Franklin, IN 46131  Public Library (Circulation Desk, Franklin, Branch) – 401 State St, Franklin, IN 46131 Comments can be provided, in writing, by the deadline of September 15th, 2026, at 5 p.m. to Barbara Davis, ADA Coordinator, in person, via email to bdavis@JohnsonCounty.in.gov , or via US Mail. In addition, the County has scheduled a meeting to solicit public input and comment on the Transition Plan, and will consist of a short presentation at the beginning of the meeting to provide information on the Transition Plan, followed by open discussion and interaction with attendees. This will be an opportunity for the community to ask questions as well as provide suggestions and comments on the draft Self-Evaluation and Transition Plan. All comments will be reviewed, considered and included in the appendix of the document. The meeting will be held in the auditorium at the County Annex building, 86 W. Court St., on September 14th, 2026, at 5:00pm. Johnson County complies with the ADA. Upon request, the County will provide written materials in appropriate alternative formats, or disability-related modification or accommodation, including auxiliary aids or services, to enable individuals with disabilities to participate in public input. Please send a written request, including your name, mailing address, phone number, and brief description of the requested accommodation at least three (3) business days prior to the close of the comment period to the ADA Coordinator in the Commissioner’s Office at the Courthouse Annex (86 W. Court St., Franklin, IN 46131).

items.title: Notice to Bidders – JC Park Banquet Hall – DUE 10/19/2026 by 10:00 a.m.
items.text: NOTICE TO BIDDERS Notice is hereby given that Johnson County, Indiana, acting by and through its Board of Commissioners, will receive sealed bids at the Office of the Auditor in Johnson County Courthouse West Annex, 86 West Court Street, Franklin, for the Johnson County Park Banquet Hall Project in Nineveh Indiana. Bids are due no later than 10:00 a.m. (local time) on Monday, October 19, 2026. Bids received after this time will be returned unopened. E- mailed or faxed bids will not be accepted. Drawings, Specifications, Instruction to Bidders, and Bid Forms will be ready September 28, 2026, and may be obtained by contacting Wes Harrison, County Project Manager, at wharrison@lhb-eng.com or (317) 431-3863. Bid security in the amount of 2% of the bid amount, including alternates, must accompany each bid in accordance with the Instruction to Bidders. Bid Security shall be in the form of a bid bond, cashier’s check, or certified check which shall be payable to the Board of Commissioners of Johnson County, Indiana. items.title: Notice to Bidders – JC Park Horse Barns Renovation Project – Due 11/9/2026 by 10:00 a.m.
items.text: NOTICE TO BIDDERS Notice is hereby given that Johnson County, Indiana, acting by and through its Board of Commissioners, will receive sealed bids at the Office of the Auditor in Johnson County Courthouse West Annex, 86 West Court Street, Franklin, for the Johnson County Park Horse Barns Renovation Project in Nineveh Indiana. Bids are due no later than 10:00 a.m. (local time) on Monday, November 9, 2026 . Bids received after this time will be returned unopened. E-mailed or faxed bids will not be accepted. Drawings, Specifications, Instruction to Bidders, and Bid Forms will be ready October 7, 2026, and may be obtained by contacting Wes Harrison, County Project Manager, at wharrison@lhb-eng.com or (317) 431-3863. Bid security in the amount of 2% of the bid amount, including alternates, must accompany each bid in accordance with the Instruction to Bidders. Bid Security shall be in the form of a bid bond, cashier’s check, or certified check which shall be payable to the Board of Commissioners of Johnson County, Indiana. The successful bidder will be required to furnish performance and payment bonds for one hundred percent (100%) of the contract price prior to the execution of contracts. There will be a non-mandatory but highly encouraged pre-bid meeting on October 15 at 10:30 a.m. at the Johnson County Park Horse Barns. The Commissioners reserve the right to accept or reject and bid and to waive any irregularities in bidding. All bids may be held for a period not to exceed ninety (90) days before awarding contracts.

Franklin Community Schools administrators are committed to the effective operation and success of our schools. Their responsibilities are broad and encompass various aspects of school management. Their key roles include:
Educational Leadership
Operational Management
Student Support

The school board plays a vital role in the governance and oversight of Franklin Community Schools. The board ensures that schools operate effectively and meet the educational needs of students. Key roles include:
Policy Development and Oversight
Financial Management
Superintendent Selection and Evaluation
Curriculum and Instruction Approval
Community Engagement and Advocacy
Facilities and Infrastructure
Accountability and Evaluation of Student Achievement
Employment Contracts and Collective Bargaining Agreements Approval
Strategic Planning
The board ensures that FCS provides high-quality education and operates in a manner that reflects our community's values and needs. The members' governance helps shape the educational landscape and directly impacts the success and well-being of students and staff.

items.title: Board of Zoning Appeals | Town of Prince’s Lakes
items.text:
Board of Zoning Appeals
The Board of Zoning Appeals meets to approve or deny variances from the development standards (such as height, bulk or area) of the zoning ordinance. They approve or deny all special exceptions, special uses, contingent uses and conditional uses pertaining to cases or the particular situations specified in the zoning ordinance.
The Board of Zoning Appeals shall hear and determine appeals from and review:
(1) any order, requirement, decision, or determination made by an administrative official, hearing officer, or staff member under the zoning ordinance;
(2) any order, requirement, decision, or determination made by an administrative board or other body except a plan commission in relation to the enforcement of the zoning ordinance; or
(3) any order, requirement, decision, or determination made by an administrative board or other body except a plan commission in relation to the enforcement of an ordinance adopted under the chapter requiring the procurement of an improvement location or occupancy permit.
Applications and the meeting and filing dates can be found in the forms below.

items.title: Park Board | Town of Prince’s Lakes
items.text:
Park Board
The Prince's Lakes Park Board was initiated in November 2023 by our Town Council to create a master plan for our parks. The master plan is a 5-year plan that is used to improve our facilities for our residents to use. The Park Board oversees the Prince's Lakes Town Hall Park, Robertson-Shay Park and their amenities. They also oversee Town events and organize them to the likeness of the Town's residents. The Park Board meets every Thursday before the Town Council Meeting.
If you would like to inquire about a Town event , or have any questions regaurding the parks, please use the contact information below, or contact Town Hall at (317) 933-2163.

Home
Town Home Page
CATALYTIC CONVERTER PACKET
CATALYTIC CONVERTER SALE REQUIREMENTS
The sale of a converter without a dealer license requires the police to inspect the converter and the vehicle it came off. This is done by cutting the converter off in the presence of law enforcement or having a law enforcement officer view the vehicle that the converter was cut off of to match the converter being sold. The law enforcement officer can complete a reporting showing that the converter has been verified as not stolen and able to be sold with the Make Model and VIN the converter was removed from. This report shall be taken to a Core Buyer of their choice and then sold.
Any law enforcement agency can inspect the vehicle and converter and complete the report. If the vehicle and converter are not present together then Edinburgh Police will not complete the report for sale.

ADA
PUBLIC NOTICE
The Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990 (“ADA”)
In accordance with the requirements of Title II of the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990 (“ADA”), The Town of Edinburgh will not discriminate against qualified individuals with disabilities on the basis of disability in its services, programs, or activities.
Employment
The Town of Edinburgh Indiana does not discriminate on the basis of disability in its hiring or employment practices and complies with all federal and state law requirements.
Effective Communication
The Town of Edinburgh Indiana will generally, upon request, provide appropriate aids and services leading to effective communication for qualified persons with disabilities so they can participate equally in town programs, services, and activities.
Modifications to Policies and Procedures
The Town of Edinburgh Indiana will make all reasonable modifications to policies and programs to ensure that people with disabilities have an equal opportunity to enjoy all of its programs, services, and activities.
Anyone who requires an auxiliary aid or service for effective communication, or a modification of policies or procedures to participate in a program, service, or activity of the town, should contact the office of the program, service or activity coordinator as soon as possible but no later than 48 hours before the scheduled event.
The ADA does not require the town to take any action that would fundamentally alter the nature of its programs or services, or impose an undue financial or administrative burden.
Complaints that a program, service, or activity of the Town of Edinburgh Indiana is not accessible to persons with disabilities should be directed to:
ADA Coordinator: Mary Patterson
Address: 107 S. Holland St.
Edinburgh, IN 46124
E-Mail: mpatterson@edinburgh.in.us
Phone: (812) 526-3510 TTY: 711
The Town of Edinburgh is working diligently toward bringing the town facilities into compliance with the ADA requirements. If anyone has any areas within town they feel are not accessible or have been denied access to due to having a disability, please see our ADA Grievance Procedures below and the ADA Grievance Form which can be filled out and returned to the Edinburgh ADA Coordinator for processing.
For more information regarding the Town of Edinburgh and the ADA, the town has an ADA Transition Plan which is available to the residents by clicking the link below.

Document Center Board & Commission Openings
Board & Commission Openings
The Town of Edinburgh has several openings on various 2027 boards and commissions starting October 5, 2026.
· Planning Commission- one board member for a 4-year term. Qualified applicants must live within Town limits and be an elected official or an employee of the Town of Edinburgh.
· Board of Metropolitan Police Commissioners- one board member for a 3-year term. Qualified applicants live within Town limits.
· Joint Planning Commission- 2 board members for a 3-year term. Qualified applicants must live within Town limits.
· Edinburgh Redevelopment Commission- 6 board members for a 1-year term. Qualified applicants must live within Town limits.
· Economic Development Board- 2 board members; 1 board member for a 1-year term and 1 board member for a 2-year term. Qualified applicants must live within Town limits.
Applications are available on the Town website by clicking here or Town Hall located at 107 S Holland Street.
Completed applications should be mailed to PO Box 65, Edinburgh, IN 46124, dropped off at the Town Hall located at 107 S Holland Street, or emailed to townhall@edinburgh.in.us by November 6, 2026.

Trafalgar Park Board
Board Members
The Trafalgar Park Board is appointed by the Town Council and plays a vital role in shaping the community’s parks and recreational spaces. The Board consists of four members who must be residents of the Town and are selected based on their interest in and knowledge of parks and recreation. No more than two members may be affiliated with the same political party unless the Town Council grants a waiver, as allowed under IND. CODE § 36-10-3-4.1 . Initial Board members served staggered terms of one, two, three, and four years, after which all members are appointed to four-year terms, with terms expiring on the first Monday in January; members continue in office until their successors are appointed, in accordance with IND. items.title: Economic Development Commission Detailed Overview
items.text: Town of Whiteland Economic Development Commission (ORD 2003-07) Primary function of an economic development commission is to permit the use of conduit financing to enable private companies to borrow funds using the municipality’s name (usually to benefit from the municipality’s tax exempt status or the TIF generated by the private development) to finance economic development projects. Composition of Membership The members of the economic development commission shall be appointed by the town executive. One (1) of the members shall be selected by the town executive, one (1) shall be nominated by the fiscal body of the county in which the town is located, and one (1) shall be nominated by the town fiscal body. (I.C. 36-7-12-6) The economic development commissioners shall take office upon their appointment, and their terms run from February 1 after their original appointment, for a period of: (1) three (3) years, if selected by the town executive; (2) two (2) years, if nominated by the town fiscal body; and (3) one (1) year, if nominated by the county fiscal body. Responsibilities An economic development commission shall investigate, study, and survey the need for additional job opportunities, industrial diversification, water services, and pollution control facilities in the unit, and shall recommend action to improve or promote job opportunities, industrial diversification, water services, and availability of pollution control facilities in the unit. Specific Responsibilities for the Town of Whiteland EDC: • make direct loans to users or developers for the cost of acquisition, construction, or installation of economic development or pollution control facilities, including land, machinery, or equipment, with the loans to be secured by the pledge of one (1) or more taxable or tax-exempt bonds or other secured or unsecured debt obligations of the users or developers; • enter into agreements with users or developers to allow the users or developers to wholly or partially construct economic development or pollution control facilities to be acquired by the unit; • issue taxable or tax -exempt bonds under this chapter for single or multiple, identified or unidentified, economic development or pollution control facilities to accomplish the purposes of this chapter, and secure their payment as provided in this chapter; • establish reserves from the proceeds of the sale of taxable or tax -exempt bonds, other funds, or both, to secure the payment of the principal and interest on the bonds; • lend or deposit the proceeds of bonds to or with a lender for the purpose of furnishing funds to the lender for the purpose of making a loan to a specifically identified developer or user for the financing of specifically identified economic development or pollution control facilities under this chapter; and • reimburse from bond proceeds expe nditures for pollution control facilities or economic development facilities. items.title: Town of Whiteland: Redevelopment Commission
items.text:
The Redevelopment Commission (RDC) is charged with encouraging economic development opportunities in Whiteland by aiding new development and the redevelopment of underutilized sites. The Commission’s primary tool is the Tax Increment Financing (TIF) district, which they oversee in conjunction with the Town Council.
Members
RDC members are appointed annually. Three are appointed by the Town Council President, and two are appointed by the Town Council. A non-voting representative of the school board also participates in Commission business.
David Hawkins – President

Meetings
Redevelopment Commission meetings are regularly scheduled on the second Thursday of each month at 6pm.
Reports
By state statute, there are two annual reports required to be prepared by every redevelopment commission. The first is required to be filed with the Town Council President by March 15 and largely describes the operations of the Commission in the previous year. The other must be filed with the Town Council by August 1 and presents the financial status of each TIF district in the town (currently, there is only one). A third report, from the Council to the Department of Local Government Finance, is due by October 1 and is a compilation of the August 1 report(s) in the state’s prescribed format.
